documents.text:
So, moving on to the method, we worked on the printed text — on two printed editions, let us say.

Sometimes there are errors that need to be corrected in the Latin text, or things that are not understood. Sometimes there are gaps because something was lost during printing, in the passage from manuscript to print, and so the text has to be critically restored with the help of two printed editions.

This is [something new] compared with when I began this kind of research. Fifteen years ago I would of course have had to go to the library. Now one edition has been digitised by Google Books, while for the 1502 edition we used the digitised print from the Bavarian State Library in Munich, which is an exceptional repository of early printed books. Seventy per cent of what we look for among incunabula, late-fifteenth-century printed books and sixteenth-century editions can be found there.
